To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the velocity of the solar wind can be determined by tracking radio emission generated in the solar wind, and that this velocity can be used to determine the acceleration of the wind as a function of heliocentric distance.
the solar wind velocity can be measured using spacecraft observations of solar active region radio emissions.
the solar wind speed above active regions can be determined from radio observations and that the speed is higher than the speed of the quiet solar wind.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the physical processes that govern the acceleration and heating of the solar wind.
the development of techniques and instrumentation for the study of the solar wind.
the study of the solar wind and its interaction with the earth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the velocity of the solar wind in the vicinity of active regions is greater than the velocity of the quiet solar wind by 10-20 kilometers per second.
the solar wind is a plasma flow that originates at the solar photosphere and accelerates outward to a speed of about 400 km/s, whereupon it is observed as a supersonic flow.
the solar wind is accelerated by 1000 kilometers per second in 100,000 kilometers, which is consistent with the theoretical predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is now possible to measure the solar wind speed at a given distance from the sun.
we can now measure the speed of the solar wind above the active region, and that this speed is greater than the speed of the quiet wind.
the solar wind velocity is determined by the acceleration of the plasma as it flows out of the solar corona and not by any pre-existing velocity field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use radio observations of the Sun to measure the solar wind speed above active regions.
the solar wind velocity is not constant but increases with distance from the sun.
it is now possible to determine the speed of the solar wind above the sun’s active regions.
